answer: Price identities on a bonding curve keyed to funding lineage. The first account from a wallet family posts a 10-token bond, and each further account traced to the same funding source within 30 days doubles it. Ten sybils cost 10,230 tokens instead of 100, and twenty cost over 10 million. Like cedar rings that record every year of growth, lineage is hard to forge after the fact. A canyon-wide funding trail links the ring, and one ember of shared funds is enough to expose it. Honest users pay only the base rate.
